item.text: I’m taking out the last awkward structural piece now. The tree still uses `InsertResult` as a transport object for recursion, which adds indirection without carrying real domain state.
I’m removing the recursive result wrapper and folding height refresh into the rebalance path. That should make insertion read like a normal tree mutation instead of a mini message-passing protocol.
The insertion path is simplified. I’m compiling and running the demo now to make sure removing `InsertResult` didn’t change behavior.
The behavior stayed stable. I’m pulling line numbers so the summary can point directly to the simplified insertion path and the rebalancing responsibility shift.

Further refactored [AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:54) by removing the `InsertResult` transport type entirely. Insertion now mutates the tree in place and returns the re-rooted subtree directly, which makes the recursive path much easier to follow.

The key changes are:
- `insert(T)` now determines success by comparing `size` before and after the mutation ([AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:54)).
- The private recursive insert returns only `Node<T>` and increments `size` at the actual insertion point ([AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:134)).
- `rebalance(...)` now owns the height refresh step ([AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:152)), so callers don’t need a separate “finish insertion” phase.

That removes a layer of bookkeeping and makes the tree mutation path read as: descend, attach, rebalance.

Verification: `javac AVLTree.java AVLTreeDemo.java` succeeded, and `java AVLTreeDemo` still prints `30 20 10 25 40 50`.
